site.name: Antelope Warm Spring
site.componentDetail: Geothermal spring, concrete-lined cistern, and documented former swimming-pool system
overview: Antelope Warm Spring is a documented low-temperature geothermal spring in Mineral County. Colorado Geological Survey records place it near 37.74333, -107.03722 and measured water near 32°C (about 90°F) during 1975 sampling.

A 1993 state field visit found the spring issuing into a concrete-lined cistern beside a wooden building containing a swimming pool. The spring water had historically been used to fill that pool, linking the natural feature to a small recreation structure.

timeline.text: Colorado geothermal investigators sampled Antelope Warm Spring and recorded water near 32°C.
The spring's location and water chemistry were published in the Colorado Geological Survey's statewide thermal-water inventory.
A Colorado Geological Survey field visit documented a concrete-lined cistern and a nearby building containing a spring-fed swimming pool.

moreHistory: The 1993 survey described the cistern as roughly 6 by 4 feet at ground level and about 5 feet deep, about 20 feet north of the pool building.
USGS later included Antelope Warm Spring in its inventory of fluorine and thermal waters in central Colorado, retaining the same mapped locality.

The mapped point identifies the documented spring and historic pool setting, not a guarantee of present public access, bathing conditions, or surviving structures. Visitors should observe current ownership, signs and closures.
